run.decision: FAIL / NO_CANDIDATE_ADMITTED / NO_ROBUST_STRATEGY_PASS. Both preregistered value-role substitutions showed positive return evidence relative to the frozen common-window V11 control but failed the frozen risk gates. IWD improved common-window CAGR from V11 8.195539% to 8.524869% and Sharpe from 0.874886 to 0.914479, beat V11 Sharpe in 5/7 fixed folds, and had paired-bootstrap P(CAGR>V11)=97.360% and P(Sharpe>V11)=99.180%. However, IWD MDD was 19.990634% and bootstrap MDD P97.5 was 26.524%, far above the frozen 10%/15% limits; cumulative 36-trial DSR probability was only 11.821%. VBR improved CAGR to 8.631507% and Sharpe to 0.906520 and also won 5/7 folds, with P(CAGR>V11)=95.205%, but P(Sharpe>V11)=88.505%, MDD was 21.618129%, bootstrap MDD P97.5 was 27.635%, and DSR was 11.084%. The trial additionally documents that restarting frozen V11 from cash at the 2004-01-30 common window materially changes its path and produces 21.291405% MDD, so this campaign is not evidence that a production V11 role substitution would retain the production V11 7.689054% MDD. Because the common-window restart design and asset substitutions were preregistered before performance, they may not be changed after seeing results. No S&P/IWD/VBR blend, substitution fraction, alternate common start, winner selection, or value timing rescue is permitted. The stable incremental return evidence from IWD is informative for future independent asset-role hypotheses, but neither current candidate is a validated strategy.

methodology.follow_up_policy: This retrospective value-role campaign ends after the two frozen substitutions are opened. Do not rescue either result by blending IWD/VBR with S&P 500, mixing IWD and VBR, changing the substitution percentage, changing the common start, switching between value ETFs, adding a third value ETF, timing the value role, changing the V11 target path, or selecting only the nicer candidate for reporting. Any materially different asset role requires a new preregistered campaign and a new trial count.
pass_fail_gates: deterministic: at least 5/7 fixed folds candidate Sharpe >= V11-CONTROL Sharpe in the same fold
deterministic: target gross <=100%, min target weight >=0, no financing or shorting
bootstrap: paired circular moving blocks against the common-window V11 control, 63 sessions, 20000 replicates, seed 20260822
PBO/winner-selection test: not applicable because neither candidate may be selected as a family winner; both are independently reported
global post-protocol DSR probability >=95% using all prior 34 formal return-seeking candidates plus both current candidates, total trial count 36
ROBUST_STRATEGY_PASS for a candidate requires every applicable deterministic, bootstrap, and global DSR gate
methodology.selection_metric: No winner selection, blend search, or survivor reporting. Each role candidate is assessed independently against the same common-window frozen V11 control. A pass by one candidate does not erase or modify the other candidate's trial count or result.

allowed_changes: F-IWD-SP500-ROLE replaces only the realized USD adjusted-close total-return series carried by the frozen V11 sp500 portfolio role with IWD; the asset option, role key, USD/CNY conversion, V11 signals and V11 target weights remain unchanged
F-VBR-SP500-ROLE performs the identical role substitution using VBR

the common evaluation starts 2004-01-30, the first available VBR adjusted-close date; V11-CONTROL is independently rerun from cash on exactly the same common window rather than compared with the longer 2002 baseline
both candidates are preregistered independently before either candidate performance is viewed and both remain permanently in G3/global multiple-testing accounting regardless of outcome
forbidden_changes: any frozen V11 signal, parameter, event date, target sizing, or target-path modification
any post-result IWD/VBR blend or blend with S&P 500
any substitution fraction other than exactly 100% of the sp500 role
any candidate selection that hides, removes, or downweights the other preregistered candidate from G3/DSR accounting
any alternative value ETF, value index, small-cap ETF, factor score, or third candidate after results
any value timing, moving average, relative-strength, valuation threshold, momentum confirmation, or regime gate
any common-evaluation-start change after performance is viewed
any leverage, financing, negative cash, or gross exposure above 100%
using future IWD/VBR returns to alter V11 signals or target weights
